# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Campbell_2023_chloroprene_mouse_pbpk")()$reference`
* Article: [Front Pharmacol 14:1223808](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2023.1223808)
* Supplement (model code, physiological tables, dose-metric summaries): [Supplementary Material](https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fphar.2023.1223808/full#supplementary-material)

Campbell et al. extend the Clewell et al. (2019) physiologically-based
pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model for inhaled beta-chloroprene (CP; 2-chloro-1,3-butadiene)
to describe the reactive oxidative metabolites formed in lung and liver and the
depletion of tissue glutathione (GSH) they cause. Parent CP is distributed over
a whole-body flow-limited PBPK structure (lung in series as the portal of entry,
then liver, kidney, rapidly- and slowly-perfused tissue and fat) and oxidised by
cytochrome P450 to two oxiranes: the stable 1-CEO ((1-chloroethenyl)oxirane) and
the unstable 2-CEO. A linked 1-CEO submodel clears 1-CEO by epoxide-hydrolase
hydrolysis and, in the mouse only, a second microsomal oxidation to a diepoxide.
The unstable 2-CEO and the diepoxide are lumped into a reactive-product (RP) pool
that reacts with GSH (second order) and with other cellular constituents (first
order). GSH follows zero-order synthesis and first-order turnover, so rising RP
production depletes GSH disproportionately as exposure increases.

This article validates the **female-mouse** parameterisation
(`Campbell_2023_chloroprene_mouse_pbpk`). The companion female-rat
parameterisation is not shipped: the paper reports the rat's 1-CEO, reactive-
product and GSH constants (Table 1) but not the rat parent-CP oxidation Vmax/Km,
which reside in the upstream Clewell et al. (2019) model and are not reproduced
here.

# Population

The model represents a single reference **female B6C3F1 mouse** of body weight
0.04 kg (the NTP 1998 time- and survival-weighted average control body weight,
Supplementary Table S2). It is a deterministic forward toxicokinetic model, not
a fit to individual data, so it carries no between-subject variability and no
residual error. Exposures are inhalation of CP vapour at the National Toxicology
Program (NTP 1998) bioassay concentrations (0, 12.8, 32 and 80 ppm) over
single-6 h and 14-day (6 h/day, 5 days/week) protocols.

The same information is available programmatically via the model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("Campbell_2023_chloroprene_mouse_pbpk")()$population`).

# Source trace

Every parameter's origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to its `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Campbell_2023_chloroprene_mouse_pbpk.R`.
The structure (ODEs) was transcribed from the acslX/Berkeley-Madonna-style
listing in the Supplementary Material; the final values from the tables.

| Group | Parameters | Source |
|-------|------------|--------|
| Physiology (flows, volumes, ventilation, cardiac output) | `qp_per_kg`, `qcc`, `qlc`..`qrc`, `vlc`..`vkc`, `vtot_b` | Supplementary Table S2 (Brown et al. 1997; Marino et al. 2006) |
| Parent-CP partition coefficients | `pb`, `plu`, `pl`, `pf`, `ps`, `pr`, `pk` | Supplementary Table S3 (Himmelstein et al. 2004) |
| Parent-CP oxidation kinetics | `vmaxc`, `km`, `vmaxclu`, `kmlu` | Supplementary Table S6 (female-mouse central value; Clewell et al. 2019) |
| 1-CEO partition coefficients | `pb1`, `plu1`, `pl1`, `pf1`, `ps1`, `pr1` | Table 1 (IndusChemFate, logKow 1.22) |
| CP->oxirane split and privileged access | `alphal`, `alphalu`, `beta` | Table 1 (Himmelstein et al. 2004; Campbell et al. 2015) |
| 1-CEO metabolism (hydrolysis + mouse oxidation) | `vmaxc1`, `km1`, `vmaxclu1`, `kmlu1`, `vmaxc1o`, `km1o`, `lloxact` | Table 1 (Himmelstein et al. 2004) |
| Reactive products and GSH | `kgshlc`, `kgshluc`, `kfeec`, `lleeact`, `kpc`, `gso`, `gsolu` | Table 1 (Clewell et al. 2001; D'Souza et al. 1988; Csanady et al. 2003) |
| Rate equations (1-CEO, RP, GSH) | `d/dt(...)` | Figure 2, Eqs 1-3; Supplementary model code |

**Units note (dimensional analysis).** CP and 1-CEO amounts are in mg; their
tissue concentrations (`a_x / (v * p)`) are mg/L and feed Michaelis-Menten terms
with Vmax in mg/h and Km in mg/L. The reactive-product and GSH states are tissue
concentrations in uM: RP production converts metabolised mass to uM/h as
`(mg/h / (g/mol)) * 1000 / L`, the GSH second-order loss `kgsh * RP * GSH` has
units `(L/umol/h) * (uM) * (uM) = uM/h`, and the first-order GSH turnover
`kp * GSH` has units `(1/h) * uM`. The RP->non-GSH term `kfee * RP` is first
order (`(1/h) * uM`); see the Errata note on its reported unit label.

# Simulation setup

The model is deterministic, so no virtual cohort is required: a single solve per
exposure scenario reproduces the published typical-value predictions. Inhalation
enters through the `conc_air_ppm` parameter (a square-wave air concentration);
`exp_hours_per_day` and `exp_days_per_week` set the exposure schedule. Body
weight `WT` is supplied as the reference female mouse (0.04 kg).

```{r sim-helper}
mod <- readModelDb("Campbell_2023_chloroprene_mouse_pbpk")
WT_mouse <- 0.04

# One deterministic solve at a given air concentration and schedule.
solve_cp <- function(ppm, tmax, by = 0.1,
                     hours_per_day = 6, days_per_week = 5) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(seq(0, tmax, by = by))
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod,
    c(WT = WT_mouse, conc_air_ppm = ppm,
      exp_hours_per_day = hours_per_day, exp_days_per_week = days_per_week),
    ev, returnType = "data.frame"
  )
}

# Lung and liver GSH baselines (uM) from the model metadata.
GSOLU <- 1500 # lung
GSO <- 7000   # liver
```

# Steady-state and mass-balance checks

With no exposure the model must hold at the reported GSH baselines indefinitely
and generate no chloroprene burden.

```{r steady-state}
ss <- solve_cp(ppm = 0, tmax = 336, by = 1)
stopifnot(
  # GSH stays at baseline (deterministic; zero-order synthesis = first-order loss)
  max(abs(ss$Cgsh_lung - GSOLU)) < 1e-4,
  max(abs(ss$Cgsh_liver - GSO)) < 1e-4,
  # no reactive product, no 1-CEO, no systemic CP without exposure
  max(ss$Crp_lung) < 1e-8,
  max(ss$Cc) < 1e-8
)
```

Chloroprene mass balance over a single 6 h exposure: everything inhaled is
accounted for as exhaled + tissue burden + metabolised.

```{r mass-balance}
mb <- solve_cp(ppm = 80, tmax = 6, by = 0.05)
e <- mb[nrow(mb), ]
tissue <- with(e, a_lung + a_liver + a_kidney + a_slow + a_rapid + a_fat)
metabolised <- with(e, a_met_liver + a_met_lung)
balance <- e$a_inhaled - (e$a_exhaled + tissue + metabolised)
# relative closure of the chloroprene mass balance
stopifnot(abs(balance) / e$a_inhaled < 1e-3)
```

# Figure 3 -- GSH depletion and reactive-product formation vs exposure

Figure 3 shows lung GSH and the reactive-product concentration at the end of a
single 6 h exposure as a function of inhaled CP. The paper reports two landmark
points for the female mouse: GSH falls 30% below baseline at **6.3 ppm** and 50%
below baseline at **14.6 ppm** (vertical lines in Figure 3).

```{r figure-3-compute}
ppm_grid <- c(seq(0, 20, by = 0.5), seq(22, 120, by = 2))
end6 <- lapply(ppm_grid, function(p) {
  s <- solve_cp(p, tmax = 6, by = 0.1)
  s[nrow(s), c("Cgsh_lung", "Crp_lung")]
})
end6 <- do.call(rbind, end6)
end6$ppm <- ppm_grid
end6$gsh_pct <- 100 * end6$Cgsh_lung / GSOLU
```

```{r figure-3-gate}
# Landmark depletion points (deterministic; reproduces the Figure 3 verticals).
gsh_at <- function(p) {
  s <- solve_cp(p, tmax = 6, by = 0.1)
  100 * s$Cgsh_lung[nrow(s)] / GSOLU
}
pct_6_3 <- gsh_at(6.3)   # paper: ~70% of baseline (30% depletion)
pct_14_6 <- gsh_at(14.6) # paper: ~50% of baseline (50% depletion)
stopifnot(
  abs(pct_6_3 - 70) < 3,
  abs(pct_14_6 - 50) < 3
)
c(ppm_6.3 = pct_6_3, ppm_14.6 = pct_14_6)
```

```{r figure-3-plot}
ggplot(end6, aes(ppm)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cgsh_lung, colour = "Lung GSH (uM)")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Crp_lung * 500, colour = "Lung RP (uM, x500)")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(6.3, 14.6), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Lung GSH (uM)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 500, name = "Lung reactive product (uM)")
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Lung GSH (uM)" = "#1b7837",
                                 "Lung RP (uM, x500)" = "#2166ac")) +
  labs(x = "Inhaled chloroprene (ppm)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Figure 3 -- end-of-6 h lung GSH and reactive product vs exposure",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Campbell et al. 2023; dashed lines at 6.3 and 14.6 ppm.") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

As GSH is consumed the reactive-product concentration rises non-linearly with
exposure: once GSH can no longer scavenge the reactive products efficiently they
accumulate, the mechanism the paper links to the dose-dependence of toxicity.

# Figure 4 -- 14-day bioassay timecourse

Figure 4 follows lung CP, 1-CEO, reactive product and GSH over the 14-day
bioassay protocol (6 h/day, 5 days/week) at the control and three bioassay
concentrations. The square-wave schedule produces rapid rises during each 6 h
exposure, partial overnight and weekend recovery of GSH, and progressively
deeper GSH depletion over the two weeks at the higher concentrations.

```{r figure-4}
concs <- c(control = 0, `12.8 ppm` = 12.8, `32 ppm` = 32, `80 ppm` = 80)
tc <- lapply(names(concs), function(nm) {
  s <- solve_cp(concs[[nm]], tmax = 336, by = 0.25)
  data.frame(
    time = s$time, exposure = nm,
    CP = s$Cc, `1-CEO` = s$Cceo1_lung,
    RP = s$Crp_lung, GSH = s$Cgsh_lung,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
})
tc <- do.call(rbind, tc)
tc$exposure <- factor(tc$exposure, levels = names(concs))

tc |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c("CP", "1-CEO", "RP", "GSH"),
                      names_to = "quantity", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::mutate(quantity = factor(quantity, levels = c("CP", "1-CEO", "RP", "GSH"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, value, colour = exposure)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~quantity, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = as_labeller(c(
               CP = "Lung-venous CP (mg/L)", `1-CEO` = "Lung 1-CEO (uM)",
               RP = "Lung reactive product (uM)", GSH = "Lung GSH (uM)"))) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = NULL, colour = "Exposure",
       title = "Figure 4 -- 14-day lung timecourse (6 h/day, 5 days/week)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Campbell et al. 2023 (female-mouse lung).")
```

# Dose metrics vs Supplementary Table S7

The paper evaluates three candidate lung dose metrics over the 14-day protocol:
total CP metabolised per gram lung per day (**Tmet**), average reactive-product
concentration (**Preact**) and average 1-CEO concentration. Supplementary Table S7
reports Monte-Carlo medians over 1000 parameter draws; the deterministic
typical-value model should land near those medians.

```{r dose-metrics}
MW <- 88.5
TSTOP <- 336
vtot <- 0.0549 + 0.0073 + 0.1 + 0.384 + 0.08098 + 0.0167
vlu <- 0.0073 * WT_mouse * (0.64398 / vtot)

metrics <- lapply(c(12.8, 32, 80), function(p) {
  s <- solve_cp(p, tmax = TSTOP, by = 0.25)
  e <- s[nrow(s), ]
  data.frame(
    ppm = p,
    Tmet = ((e$a_met_lung * 1000 / MW) / (vlu * 1000)) / (TSTOP / 24), # umol/g/day
    Preact = e$auc_rp_lung / TSTOP,       # uM
    CEO1 = e$auc_ceo1_lung / TSTOP        # uM
  )
})
metrics <- do.call(rbind, metrics)

published <- data.frame(
  ppm = c(12.8, 32, 80),
  Tmet_pub = c(0.824, 1.26, 1.61),
  Preact_pub = c(0.247, 0.495, 0.883),
  CEO1_pub = c(5.74e-4, 1.18e-3, 2.51e-3)
)
cmp <- merge(metrics, published, by = "ppm")
cmp |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    "Inhaled (ppm)" = ppm,
    "Tmet (sim)" = round(Tmet, 3), "Tmet (S7 median)" = Tmet_pub,
    "Preact (sim)" = round(Preact, 3), "Preact (S7 median)" = Preact_pub,
    "1-CEO (sim)" = signif(CEO1, 3), "1-CEO (S7 median)" = CEO1_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated 14-day lung dose metrics vs Supplementary Table S7 medians.")
```

```{r dose-metrics-gate}
# Tmet and Preact (the paper's two cross-species-consistent metrics) land
# within ~10% of the Table S7 medians. 1-CEO is more sensitive to the Table 1
# vs Table S6 metabolite-parameter discrepancy and runs ~25% high -- well
# inside its reported ~40% Monte-Carlo CV -- so it carries a wider bound.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(cmp$Tmet - cmp$Tmet_pub) / cmp$Tmet_pub < 0.12),
  all(abs(cmp$Preact - cmp$Preact_pub) / cmp$Preact_pub < 0.12),
  all(abs(cmp$CEO1 - cmp$CEO1_pub) / cmp$CEO1_pub < 0.35)
)
```

Both Tmet and Preact reproduce the published medians within a few percent, and
1-CEO stays below 0.4% of the reactive-product concentration throughout, matching
the paper's observation that 1-CEO is a minor fraction of total reactive
metabolism and a poor cross-species dose metric.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Female-rat parameterisation not shipped.** The paper gives the rat 1-CEO,
  reactive-product and GSH constants (Table 1) but not the rat parent-CP
  oxidation Vmax/Km, which live in the upstream Clewell et al. (2019) model and
  are not reproduced here. Only the fully-specified female-mouse model is
  packaged; the rat can be added once the upstream parent-CP kinetics are on
  hand.
- **Parent-CP oxidation kinetics (`vmaxc`, `km`, `vmaxclu`, `kmlu`).** These are
  inherited from Clewell et al. (2019) and taken from the female-mouse central
  values in Supplementary Table S6, the only on-disk source that reports them.
- **`beta` (privileged-access fraction) = 0.33.** Table 1 reports 0.33 as the
  fraction of formed 1-CEO available for distribution/metabolism. The text
  describes the complementary 67% of butadiene-derived epoxybutene as further
  metabolised by co-localised epoxide hydrolase (Campbell et al. 2015); the
  structural term multiplies the available fraction, so 0.33 is used. The
  supplementary code listing carries 0.67 in the opposite (diverted-fraction)
  sense; the mouse GSH-depletion curve reproduces Figure 3 only with 0.33 as
  the available fraction.
- **`kfeec` unit.** The maintainers read Table 1's unit label for KFEEC
  (L/umol/h) as a copy of the neighbouring KGSH unit: the text states KFEE is a
  first-order rate constant, Figure 2 Eq 2 uses it first order, and the rate
  equation is dimensionally consistent only if KFEE is 1/h. The value 35 is
  therefore applied as a first-order rate (1/h).
- **Table 1 vs Table S6 metabolite parameters.** The 1-CEO hydrolysis and
  oxidation Vmax/Km differ by about 15-18% between Table 1 (used here, as the
  explicit "parameters used in the CP metabolite submodel") and the Table S6
  Monte-Carlo central values. This is the main source of the ~25% high 1-CEO
  dose metric; Tmet and Preact are unaffected.
- **Deterministic, no variability.** The model is a recoded literature PBPK
  model evaluated against in vitro kinetics and bioassay dose-response, not a
  fit to individual data, so it carries no IIV and no residual error. The
  Supplementary Table S6/S7 Monte-Carlo analysis varies the parameters for an
  uncertainty assessment but is not between-subject variability.
- **Convention deviations.** As a whole-body PBPK model it uses descriptive
  per-tissue state names (declared via `paper_specific_compartment_pattern`) and
  non-log-transformed physiological constants rather than the canonical PK
  parameterisation; both are standard for the PBPK models in this library.
- No correction notice for this article was found as of 2026-10-27.
